description: Space Technology is a crucial pillar of India's scientific and technological advancement. This topic covers the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), its launch vehicles, key satellites, and historic space missions, optimized for rapid revision for competitive exams.

sections.title: History of Indian Space Programme
sections.description: Important milestones and foundational years in the development of space research in India.

historical_events.significance: The Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR) was set up under the visionary leadership of Dr. Vikram Sarabhai.
The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was formed, superseding INCOSPAR, to institutionalize space activities in India.
The Government of India established the Space Commission and the Department of Space (DoS), bringing ISRO under the DoS.
Aryabhata was India's first artificial satellite, successfully launched using a Soviet Union launch vehicle.

sections.title: Launch Vehicles of ISRO
sections.description: Rocket systems developed by ISRO to place satellites into various orbits around the Earth or into deep space.

key_concepts.explanation: Often called the 'Workhorse of ISRO', it is a highly reliable four-stage rocket primarily used to launch remote sensing satellites into Sun-synchronous polar orbits.
A three-stage rocket featuring an indigenous cryogenic upper stage, designed to launch heavier communication satellites into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO).
Formerly known as GSLV Mk III, it is ISRO's heaviest and most powerful launch vehicle. It successfully launched the Chandrayaan-3 spacecraft.
A low-cost, quick-turnaround launch vehicle developed to place small, micro, or nano satellites into Low Earth Orbit (LEO).

sections.title: Major Space Missions of ISRO
sections.description: Key planetary, lunar, and solar missions undertaken by ISRO for space exploration.

historical_events.significance: India's first lunar mission, which made the groundbreaking discovery of water molecules on the Moon's surface.
Made India the first country in the world to successfully reach the Martian orbit in its very first attempt.
Successfully made a soft landing on the Moon's South Pole on August 23, 2023. India became the first country to achieve this feat (celebrated as National Space Day).
India's first dedicated solar mission, placed in a halo orbit around the Lagrange Point 1 (L1) to study the Sun's atmosphere.

key_concepts.explanation: India's upcoming first manned spaceflight program, aiming to send Indian astronauts (Gaganauts) to Low Earth Orbit (LEO) and bring them back safely.

sections.title: Important Space Orbits
sections.description: Specific paths around the Earth where satellites are placed based on their functions.

key_concepts.explanation: An orbit ranging from 160 km to 2,000 km above the Earth's surface. The International Space Station (ISS) and most Earth observation satellites are in LEO.
A circular orbit 35,786 km exactly above the Earth's equator. Satellites here revolve at the same speed as Earth's rotation, appearing stationary from the ground. Ideal for telecommunication.
An orbit in which a satellite passes above or nearly above both poles of the Earth. Widely used for Earth mapping, spying, and weather forecasting.

sections.title: Major Space Centres of India
sections.description: Key ISRO facilities and their primary locations across India.

The primary spaceport and launch centre of India.
The lead centre for designing, developing, and manufacturing satellites.
Focuses on the design of space-borne instruments and payloads for ISRO missions.

key_associations.associated_with: Hassan, Karnataka and Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh
key_associations.extra_info: Monitors and controls all the geostationary and geosynchronous satellites of ISRO.

sections.title: Important Facts of Space Science
sections.description: Crucial one-liner 'firsts' and general knowledge facts highly relevant for objective exams.

important_facts.fact: Dr. Vikram Sarabhai is universally acknowledged as the 'Father of the Indian Space Programme'.
Wing Commander Rakesh Sharma was the first Indian to travel to space aboard the Soviet spacecraft T-11 in 1984.
Yuri Gagarin (Soviet Union) became the first human to journey into outer space in 1961, and Neil Armstrong (USA) was the first person to walk on the Moon in 1969.
Sputnik-1, launched by the Soviet Union in 1957, was the world's first artificial satellite.
NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) is India's own indigenous independent regional navigation satellite system.
